nonRoot.surfaceContract: Identity, shared clear, private table publication, log initialization and pre-phase CPU/kernel setup are retained direct interfaces.
Primary/peer-specific setup, domain and clock setup, callback/tick publication. Phase2 callback cells are 0x4004f114/0x400df0d4.
Scan 120 creation records/id-map words; flags bit1 causes preparation; write T+24 stack top, T+28 domain trampoline; insert priority queue and bitmap. Explicit activation is a separate producer.
Nonreturning mode/context transfer; selected node becomes current, C+32 supplies CP15 task identity, SP=T+24, PC=T+28; null selection has separate idle-stack loop at stacks0xa0000/0x130000.
A32 SVC written CPSR fields0x53; cleanup LR; clear T+48; r0=C argument, r1=T,r2=C; load C entry into PC; stack top rather than restored exception frame.
SPSR/LDM exception resume differs from first entry. Bounded idle qualification observes interrupt frame and restored task SP/LR/CPSR/PC.

SVC0 decodes interrupted state and branches to incoming r0, with SP-16 and LR0. Diagnostic reason/frame paths can invoke published callbacks. Main restore consumes current banked SPSR; FIQ explicitly restores SPSR. Actual SVC0 targets, genuine restore gate producer and frame-writer closure remain open.
Read count0x4dacc/0xdda90, pair24-byte static records0x4005ef78/0x400eef38 with live records0x4005928c/0x400e924c; flag bit1 activates. Earlier pre-phase registration uses id120.

Shared idle repeats WFI/backedge. Standby requires whole event output word1, masks IRQ, cleans/invalidates caches, disables caches, saves/masks IRQ banks, WFI, restores banks/IRQ and unconditionally enables caches. Low-address helpers run on the executing core.

objectConsumers.surfaceContract: 120 descriptors publish id, eight C-field pointers and T+24/+28 pointers; C stride40,T stride56. Root+0x174 publishes shared tick0x400c0800; +0x1628 is stack top, not callable.

Select root by current identity; descriptor root+0x184+44*(id-1) yields pointer to C+8 entry. Nonzero entry admits root+0x190+44*(id-1), pointer to C+20 stack base. Reads four stack words and compares replicated id byte. Returns/reports -64 on failure. Periodic callback cycles ids1..104.

Selected-root+0x174 is loaded then dereferenced. Getter writes caller output; elapsed adapter returns ten times wrapping tick difference; sampling combines tick/MMIO under critical sections. Exact sites are source inspection, not additional runtime qualification.

Create/activate/auto-ready/scheduler/first-entry/resume read C/T links, priority/status bytes, saved SP/PC, scheduler domains and current/selected words. Retaining them preserves raw layout obligations.

deviceLaws.grounded: Stock IRQ/return and bounded idle cycles are observed in pinned model; model installs controllers0xfffb3000/0xfffb4000 with active-bitmap arbitration.
deviceLaws.missing: Physical arbitration, nesting, priority, pending/EOI/level relatch and standby routing are not qualified.
scenarios: Existing: retained/owned idle,12 B cycles and1 A cycle
Proposed: equal/unequal priority simultaneous sources, nesting, asserted-level reentry, pending clear versus EOI, IRQ/FIQ masks

deviceLaws.grounded: Stock reads reload/count0xfff91004/0xfff91000 and stores their subtraction. Qualified comparison binds actual30000-23632 and30000-23630 transactions. Hardware log tick rate is separately bounded.
deviceLaws.missing: Physical frequency, divider/control semantics, IRQ fanout, reload/wrap races and scheduling deadlines remain unqualified.
scenarios: Existing: loader elapsed provenance and natural menu route
Existing: idle timer/IRQ wake in modeled system
Proposed: reload boundary, wrap, simultaneous read/write, timeout expiry and cancellation

deviceLaws.grounded: Source sequence reads0xfffb4080..0xfffb408c, disables via0xfffb40a0..0xfffb40ac, enables fourth-bank bit0x01000000, WFI, disables bit and restores saved words. Model treats enable writes as OR and disable writes as clear.
deviceLaws.missing: B93 concrete mask1 flag producer, hardware source identity, ordering/routing/acknowledgment and completed standby restore cycle remain open. Model source120 numbering is not hardware identification.
scenarios: Existing: B93 initial unsatisfied wait/block only
Proposed: naturally produced exact flag1, standby WFI wake and complete restoration; flag3 must not enter standby

deviceLaws.grounded: Word LDREX/STREX stock loops: nonzero try-lock returns-1; failed exclusive store retries; successful store executes CP15 ordering operation. Natural uncontended lock0->2->0 and release failure behavior are evidenced.
deviceLaws.missing: Physical reservation granule, alias invalidation, peer writes, exceptions/CLREX and memory-order/coherence behavior remain unqualified.
scenarios: Proposed: concurrent cores, alias store, intervening IRQ, failed STREX and ordered wake

deviceLaws.grounded: Installer calls0x42634(0x96bd20,32) after root stores; selected arm cleans/invalidates one line. Task fill precedes cache call. Standby uses whole-cache and cache-enable helpers.
deviceLaws.missing: Silicon cache geometry/coherence, peer publication visibility, aliases/TCM interactions and complete standby cache transition effects remain unqualified.
scenarios: Existing: installer/critical/task-storage alias readback in pinned model
Proposed: root/descriptor publication through retained peer consumption, executable publication and cache-disable/enable standby cycle

deviceLaws.grounded: Completion store precedes DSB in A source; B accepts any nonzero. Peer bootstrap model uses one-shot software line120 release. Task activation may notify through0x433e4/0xd33e4.
deviceLaws.missing: Physical task wake/notification register semantics, ordering/acknowledgment, lost wake/race behavior and cache visibility are not established by bootstrap release.
scenarios: Existing: natural/held/delayed peer bootstrap and installer/loader completion
Proposed: remote ready/wakeup while peer idle, multiple notifications, mask/unmask and no-lost-wake contention

remainingClosure: All-image direct/computed/Thumb/tail/alias root-call and object-pointer provenance census remains open; named caller lists are lower bounds.
SVC0 target producers, genuine diagnostic restore producers and all exception/scheduler frame writers remain open.
Complete deletion/reuse/reclamation, priority scheduling, synchronization, timeout and cancellation ABI/error/lifetime contracts remain open.
Root1 publication precedes late initialization; first actual retained consumer and committed pointer/slot lifetime need independent evidence.
Each missing contract/device law blocks its replacement family, not continued research on other RTOS families.
